We’ve collaborated closely over the past 18 months on high-stakes consulting projects, where Xiomara’s ability to bridge complex technical challenges with client needs was consistently impressive. Her daily work often involved leading deep dives into legacy systems, translating vague requirements into scalable solutions, and mentoring junior engineers through ambiguous problems. I’ve observed her tackle everything from optimizing PostgreSQL query performance under tight deadlines to architecting microservices that scaled seamlessly across distributed teams. Her Go implementations for critical backend services once reduced latency by 40% in a production environment, a change that directly impacted user retention metrics.  

One standout moment came during a multi-week sprint to refactor a monolith into microservices. Xiomara took ownership of the payment processing module, designing a REST API that integrated with third-party systems while maintaining strict compliance standards. Her Python scripts for data migration automated what would have taken weeks of manual work, allowing the team to focus on core functionality. She also championed Docker for containerization, ensuring consistent environments across dev and prod without sacrificing security.  

Xiomara’s strength lies in her quiet reliability and analytical mindset. She’ll often spend hours debugging a single issue, but her patience and attention to detail ensure solutions are robust and sustainable. Her work ethic is unshakable—she’ll push through late nights to meet deadlines without compromising quality. I’m confident she’ll thrive in any technical leadership role, bringing both technical depth and a collaborative spirit to every team she joins.
